answer: Staked identity bonds blunt sybil attacks: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, and that stake is pressed into each action like a quill signature on a shared ledger. To run a thousand fake identities an attacker must fund a thousand bonds at once, climbing a steep cost mesa rather than cresting one cheap peak, and any agent caught misbehaving forfeits its deposit. Honest agents reclaim their bond, so a thread of accountability ties each persona to real, slashable capital instead of free names.
